meta.title: Business Negotiation and Conflict Resolution
meta.one_liner: Three mornings of live negotiation simulations, each followed by a debrief and a short lecture
meta.blurb: I co-taught this course with philosopher David Emmanuel Gray four times between 2014 and 2016. Each morning starts with a negotiation that participants play against each other in randomly assigned pairs or groups, then we debrief the actual results before any theory. The arc runs from a two-party job offer, to a property deal where the money alone has no zone of agreement, to a six-party commodity auction where coalitions decide who wins. Participants leave with BATNA, ZOPA, reservation and target prices, and a plan for dealing with hard bargainers.
meta.scale: 91 participants from 15 organizations in the November 2014 run

schedule.topic: New Recruit: an eight-issue job negotiation and debrief
schedule.note: Recruiter and candidate pairs negotiate a contract scored in points, then we compare every pair's outcome

slides.caption: Each issue is worth points, and the two sides value them differently
The Pareto frontier: creating value versus claiming it
Party B could have done better without making Party A worse off
Compatible and integrative issues: find the trades
Grow the value first, then divide it
Starting salaries of men in one MBA class were 7.6% higher than women's. What caused it?
The compounding cost of not negotiating a first salary
Your BATNA is your most important source of power
Graphical negotiation analysis: the zone of possible agreement
Review and prioritize your interests and your partner's

schedule.topic: Problem solving: managing empathy and assertiveness, with the West Bay Lagoon property negotiation
schedule.note: Lecture and debrief led by David Emmanuel Gray

slides.caption: Every negotiation is three negotiations: substance, process, and relationship
The structural change model of escalation
The dual concern model: assertiveness and empathy are not opposites
Problem solving means exchanging conclusions, interpretations, and what each side noticed
West Bay Lagoon: a buyer and a seller of a Doha bed and breakfast

schedule.topic: Negotiation jujitsu and the hard bargainer

slides.caption: Fourteen hardball tactics and dirty tricks to recognize
Responding to hardball: know yourself, prepare yourself, change the game
Turn criticism into problem solving with questions
Good cop, bad cop: name the tactic and it loses its force
Remember your power: the BATNA does not change because the other side shouts

schedule.topic: Commodity Purchase: a six-party negotiation over a scarce supply
schedule.note: One seller, five buyers, thirty minutes; debrief by me

slides.caption: One seller of 100,000 pheasant eggs and five potential buyers
Who purchased the eggs?
What were the interests of all the parties at the table?
Coalitions: when parties cooperate to claim a share of the reward
Lessons: do not anchor on your minimum, and look past positions

assignments.name: Negotiation simulations
assignments.description: Three graded-by-outcome simulations (New Recruit, West Bay Lagoon, Commodity Purchase). Results from every pair or group go up on the screen in the debrief so participants can see the full range of deals the same facts produced.
